themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key. There is no stable number to grade your work against, and the thing you are measuring often shifts while you measure it, so every model starts by building a small truth set of its own or by saying plainly that the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: Answer engine optimization answers call the model's own week-to-week drift bigger than any intervention, cross-channel incrementality calls the platform an adaptive agent that optimizes against your holdout, and identity resolution and B2B buying-group signal both stall on the lack of a verified answer key.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what will happen next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control is before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Every answer on safe agent execution builds a proxy or gateway in front of martech writes with hard spend and audience caps, downstream consent answers put one checkpoint in front of all data egress, and journey orchestration answers make every channel check a shared contact log before sending.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Several problems stall because the party holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can make them. The blocker is money and politics, inside the company as well as outside, so the models try to make honesty or cooperation pay instead of writing another rule.
themes.evidence: Agentic traffic answers offer fast lanes and price perks so declaring beats spoofing, ad platforms in cross-channel incrementality and ad supply integrity control both the treatment and the evidence, channel owners in journey orchestration are paid to keep sending, and semantic context layer answers call conflicting definitions of customer a political settlement rather than a modeling gap.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch behavior from outside and estimate whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: Downstream consent and deletion answers describe ad platforms and agency segments as black boxes with no accepted test for removing a person from an already-trained model, ad supply integrity answers note that faking supply is cheap while verifying it costs real money, and agentic traffic answers say the delegating human is never present on the wire.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning, context, and what counts as a good outcome, and no rule set captures that fully. So the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box rather than trying to remove it.
themes.evidence: Generative content governance answers all build an approved-claims registry and constrain what can be said because deciding whether evidence supports a claim is a contextual judgment experts themselves dispute, semantic context layer answers argue two teams can both be right about revenue, and journey orchestration answers say globally optimal has no definition anyone will commit to.
